descVi: Y tế, dinh dưỡng, thể chất, sức khỏe tinh thần và lối sống lành mạnh.

words.definitionEn: Different from what is usual or expected, often causing concern.
words.exampleDailyEn: The mechanic noticed an abnormal noise from the engine.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular medical screening can detect abnormal changes before they develop into conditions that require complex treatment.

words.definitionEn: Having a helpful or positive effect.
words.exampleDailyEn: A short walk after lunch is beneficial for digestion.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to green spaces is particularly beneficial to urban residents who have limited opportunities for outdoor exercise.

words.definitionEn: Having or showing plenty of energy and enthusiasm.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our energetic puppy chased a ball around the garden.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity can help office workers feel more energetic and maintain concentration throughout the day.

words.definitionEn: the ability to see
words.exampleDailyEn: My new glasses have made my vision much clearer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Urban planners need a clear vision of how expanding cities can remain both liveable and environmentally sustainable.

words.definitionEn: a condition involving persistent sadness and loss of interest
words.exampleDailyEn: Her doctor recommended regular counselling to help manage depression.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improving access to mental health services can help people with depression receive timely support and appropriate treatment.

words.definitionEn: An expert who studies the mind or helps with psychological problems.
words.exampleDailyEn: The psychologist helped me understand why exams made me anxious.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A school psychologist can support students whose emotional difficulties interfere with learning and social development.

words.definitionEn: A return to health or a normal condition.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her recovery was slow, but she could walk again.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Economic recovery depends partly on restoring consumer confidence and supporting small businesses through difficult periods.

words.definitionEn: Relating to sex or physical attraction between people.
words.exampleDailyEn: The clinic offers confidential advice about sexual health.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can provide age-appropriate sexual health education to help young people make informed decisions.

words.definitionEn: to experience a process, change, or treatment
words.exampleDailyEn: My uncle will undergo knee surgery early next week.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many coastal cities will undergo significant changes as rising sea levels force governments to reconsider urban planning.

words.definitionEn: To become larger or rounder, or make something do so.
words.exampleDailyEn: My ankle began to swell after I twisted it.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Seasonal tourism can swell the population of coastal towns, placing additional pressure on local water supplies.

words.definitionEn: a young person developing from a child into an adult
words.exampleDailyEn: The club offers cooking classes for adolescents after school.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity can improve adolescent mental health and support the development of lasting social connections.

words.definitionEn: Medicines used to treat infections caused by bacteria.
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor prescribed antibiotics for my ear infection.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Overusing antibiotics can make bacterial infections harder to treat, creating a serious challenge for public health.

words.definitionEn: A chemical element needed for strong bones and teeth
words.exampleDailyEn: This yoghurt provides calcium for healthy bones and teeth.
words.exampleIeltsEn: School meals should include adequate sources of calcium to support children's bone development during periods of rapid growth.

words.definitionEn: An extra problem that makes a situation harder to manage
words.exampleDailyEn: A delayed train added another complication to our journey.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular medical checkups can help detect complications early and improve outcomes for patients with chronic conditions.

words.definitionEn: The state of being awake and aware of your surroundings
words.exampleDailyEn: He regained consciousness shortly after the ambulance arrived.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Environmental education can raise public consciousness of how everyday consumption affects natural resources and biodiversity.

words.definitionEn: to make a disease disappear or someone healthy again
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor said these tablets could cure the infection.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although medical research has advanced considerably, scientists have not yet found a cure for every disease.

words.definitionEn: to identify an illness by examining symptoms and test results
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor diagnosed asthma after checking my breathing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: New screening technologies can help doctors diagnose certain diseases before serious symptoms appear.

words.definitionEn: Protected against a particular disease.
words.exampleDailyEn: The vet explained that vaccination would make our puppy immune.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although technology creates new opportunities, no industry is completely immune to the effects of economic change.

words.definitionEn: to cause a person or organism to develop an infection
words.exampleDailyEn: One sick rabbit can infect the others in its cage.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Viruses can infect vulnerable patients more easily when hospitals lack effective hygiene measures and adequate ventilation.

words.definitionEn: able to spread disease between people or organisms
words.exampleDailyEn: His infectious laugh soon had everyone at the table smiling.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improved sanitation and access to clean water are essential for preventing infectious diseases in densely populated communities.

words.definitionEn: To put a substance into something using a needle or pressure.
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse will inject the medicine into my arm.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public investment can inject new energy into declining towns by supporting local businesses and improving transport.

words.definitionEn: Either of two organs that filter blood and produce urine.
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor checked his kidneys during a routine examination.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public health campaigns should explain how managing blood pressure can help prevent kidney disease.

words.definitionEn: An organ that processes nutrients and removes harmful substances from blood.
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor explained how the liver keeps us healthy.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public health campaigns should explain how a balanced diet can support the liver and reduce disease risks.

words.definitionEn: Either of the two chest organs used for breathing.
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor listened to my lungs through a stethoscope.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Long periods of exposure to polluted air can damage the lungs and increase the risk of respiratory disease.

words.definitionEn: A body part that performs a particular function.
words.exampleDailyEn: The heart is an organ that pumps blood.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public awareness campaigns can encourage organ donation and help reduce waiting times for patients needing transplants.

words.definitionEn: The act of intentionally causing one's own death.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our local centre offers free workshops on suicide prevention.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Suicide prevention requires accessible mental health services, supportive communities, and responsible reporting in the media.

words.definitionEn: a doctor trained to perform operations
words.exampleDailyEn: The surgeon explained the operation before I went home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rural hospitals often struggle to recruit experienced surgeons, which can delay essential treatment for local residents.

words.definitionEn: larger than normal because of injury or illness
words.exampleDailyEn: My ankle was swollen after I fell during practice.
words.exampleIeltsEn: After several days of heavy rain, the swollen river threatened homes built close to its banks.

words.definitionEn: a blood vessel that carries blood towards the heart
words.exampleDailyEn: A blue vein was visible beneath his wrist.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular movement helps blood flow through the veins and may reduce health risks associated with prolonged sitting.

words.meaningVi: Một chất cần thiết với số lượng nhỏ để tăng trưởng và hoạt động khỏe mạnh
words.definitionEn: A substance needed in small amounts for healthy growth and functioning.
words.exampleDailyEn: These fresh oranges are a good source of vitamin C.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A varied diet usually provides the vitamins people need without requiring them to take supplements.

words.definitionEn: able to spread between people, like an illness or emotion
words.exampleDailyEn: Her laughter was catching, and soon everyone was smiling.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although enthusiasm can be catching, public health campaigns also need clear evidence to encourage lasting behavioural change.

words.definitionEn: Sudden pain caused by a muscle tightening involuntarily.
words.exampleDailyEn: A sudden cramp in my calf stopped me swimming.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Excessively strict classroom rules may cramp students' creativity and discourage them from exploring unfamiliar ideas.

words.definitionEn: Causing death or likely to cause death.
words.exampleDailyEn: These pretty mushrooms can be deadly if you eat them.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improved access to clean drinking water can prevent deadly diseases in communities with inadequate sanitation.

words.definitionEn: A state of extreme physical or mental tiredness.
words.exampleDailyEn: After the long hike, he fell asleep from exhaustion.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Persistent exhaustion among healthcare workers can reduce the quality of patient care and increase staff turnover.

words.definitionEn: The ability to see
words.exampleDailyEn: My grandfather still has excellent eyesight without wearing glasses.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular eye examinations can identify conditions that may damage eyesight if they are left untreated.

words.definitionEn: Causing someone's death.
words.exampleDailyEn: These wild mushrooms can be fatal if you eat them.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Lower speed limits near schools can reduce the risk of fatal accidents involving pedestrians and cyclists.

words.definitionEn: causing or likely to cause damage or injury
words.exampleDailyEn: Too much direct sunlight can be harmful to your skin.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Stricter controls on industrial waste could reduce the harmful effects of water pollution on local ecosystems.

words.definitionEn: Something that could cause harm, damage, or an accident.
words.exampleDailyEn: That loose cable is a hazard near the stairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Poorly stored industrial chemicals pose a serious health hazard to workers and residents in nearby communities.

words.definitionEn: to focus your mind calmly, often as a mental exercise
words.exampleDailyEn: I meditate for ten minutes before breakfast each morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some employers encourage staff to meditate during breaks as a way of managing workplace stress.

words.definitionEn: Activities done for enjoyment and relaxation when not working.
words.exampleDailyEn: I swim for recreation at the local leisure centre.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to green spaces encourages outdoor recreation and can improve both physical health and mental wellbeing.

words.definitionEn: To shake slightly because of cold, fear, or excitement
words.exampleDailyEn: I shivered while waiting outside in my thin jacket.
words.exampleIeltsEn: People may shiver when exposed to low temperatures, as muscle movements help the body generate heat.

words.definitionEn: pressure or difficulty that tests someone's strength or resources
words.exampleDailyEn: I strained my back while lifting that heavy box.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rapid population growth puts considerable strain on public services, particularly housing and healthcare in large cities.

words.definitionEn: Physical or mental pain experienced by people or animals.
words.exampleDailyEn: The medicine eased her suffering and helped her sleep.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improving access to clean water can reduce human suffering in communities affected by prolonged drought.

words.definitionEn: unable to see, hear, or respond because awareness is lost
words.exampleDailyEn: The unconscious patient was breathing steadily beneath a blanket.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Unconscious bias can influence recruitment decisions, even when employers aim to treat all applicants fairly.

words.definitionEn: To give a vaccine that helps protect against a disease.
words.exampleDailyEn: The vet will vaccinate our puppy during today's appointment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public health programmes aim to vaccinate vulnerable populations and reduce the spread of infectious diseases.

words.definitionEn: extremely important or necessary
words.exampleDailyEn: A warm coat is vital on these freezing mornings.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Reliable public transport plays a vital role in reducing urban congestion and improving access to employment.

words.definitionEn: To bring food or liquid from the stomach through the mouth.
words.exampleDailyEn: The rough boat ride made several passengers vomit.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Patients who vomit repeatedly may become dehydrated and should seek medical advice if symptoms persist.

words.definitionEn: An injury involving damage to skin or other body tissue.
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse gently cleaned the wound on my knee.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to clean water and basic medical supplies is essential for treating wounds and preventing infection.

words.definitionEn: Very serious or intense.
words.exampleDailyEn: The village faced an acute water shortage last summer.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An acute shortage of affordable housing forces many young workers to live far from their workplaces.

words.definitionEn: Continuing for a long time, especially a medical condition
words.exampleDailyEn: Gentle swimming helps her manage her chronic back pain.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Chronic staff shortages can reduce the quality of healthcare and increase pressure on existing medical workers.

words.definitionEn: A lack of enough of something necessary.
words.exampleDailyEn: A blood test revealed that I had an iron deficiency.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Nutritional deficiency among children can affect physical growth and reduce their ability to concentrate at school.

words.definitionEn: extreme tiredness caused by effort, stress, or illness
words.exampleDailyEn: After the long hike, fatigue made my legs shake.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Persistent fatigue can reduce employees' concentration and increase the likelihood of accidents in the workplace.

words.definitionEn: The beginning of something, especially something unpleasant.
words.exampleDailyEn: The sudden onset of rain sent us running indoors.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity may delay the onset of certain chronic diseases and improve overall wellbeing.

words.definitionEn: easily affected or harmed by something
words.exampleDailyEn: These young plants are particularly susceptible to frost damage.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Children may be more susceptible to online advertising because they lack experience in evaluating commercial claims.

words.definitionEn: Related to mental processes such as learning, remembering, and understanding.
words.exampleDailyEn: These puzzles help my grandmother keep her cognitive skills sharp.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity may support cognitive development in children and help older adults maintain their memory.

words.definitionEn: Inflammation of the liver, sometimes caused by a virus.
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse explained how vaccination can prevent some hepatitis infections.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public health programmes can reduce hepatitis transmission through vaccination, screening, and improved access to safe medical care.

words.definitionEn: A medical doctor, especially one treating illness without surgery.
words.exampleDailyEn: The physician listened carefully as I described my symptoms.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to a qualified physician remains limited in remote areas, contributing to significant inequalities in healthcare.

words.definitionEn: a group of symptoms that occur together in a condition
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor explained how the syndrome affects sleep.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Early recognition of a syndrome can help healthcare professionals provide appropriate support and manage symptoms more effectively.

words.definitionEn: To move an organ or plant into a new location.
words.exampleDailyEn: We transplant the seedlings once their roots are strong.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Advances in medicine have made it possible to transplant organs successfully and improve patients' quality of life.

words.definitionEn: an abnormal mass of cells growing in the body
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor explained that the tumour was not cancerous.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Early detection of a tumour can improve treatment options, although outcomes depend on its type and location.

words.definitionEn: Cause someone or something serious suffering or difficulty
words.exampleDailyEn: Seasonal allergies afflict my brother whenever the flowers bloom.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Water shortages continue to afflict rural communities, limiting agricultural production and increasing the burden on local families.

words.definitionEn: An illness, especially one that is not serious.
words.exampleDailyEn: The pharmacist suggested a remedy for my stomach ailment.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Treating minor ailments at local clinics can reduce pressure on hospitals and improve access to healthcare.

words.definitionEn: to make pain, suffering, or a problem less severe
words.exampleDailyEn: A warm bath helped alleviate the ache in my shoulders.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Expanding affordable housing could alleviate pressure on low-income families and reduce the risk of homelessness.

words.definitionEn: A short period of illness or intense activity
words.exampleDailyEn: A bout of flu kept me home all week.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular exercise may help reduce bouts of anxiety and improve overall mental health among university students.

words.definitionEn: not having enough of something necessary
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor said my diet was deficient in iron.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Communities with deficient healthcare services often face greater difficulties in preventing disease and supporting older residents.

words.definitionEn: The process of becoming worse in condition or quality.
words.exampleDailyEn: Cracks in the ceiling showed the building's gradual deterioration.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A deterioration in urban air quality can increase respiratory illness and place additional pressure on healthcare services.

words.definitionEn: Harm or damage caused to someone or something.
words.exampleDailyEn: He works late, often to the detriment of his sleep.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Prioritising short-term profits to the detriment of environmental protection can create substantial costs for future generations.

words.definitionEn: To completely remove or destroy something harmful.
words.exampleDailyEn: We removed every root to eradicate weeds from the garden.
words.exampleIeltsEn: International vaccination programmes aim to eradicate infectious diseases by ensuring that vulnerable populations receive adequate protection.

words.definitionEn: Lacking physical strength, energy, or intensity.
words.exampleDailyEn: After the illness, he felt too feeble to cook.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Feeble enforcement of environmental regulations allows some factories to continue polluting rivers without facing meaningful consequences.

words.definitionEn: to strengthen a place or structure against attack or damage
words.exampleDailyEn: We used sandbags to fortify the wall before the storm.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Manufacturers can fortify staple foods with essential vitamins to help prevent nutritional deficiencies in vulnerable populations.

words.definitionEn: able to cause death
words.exampleDailyEn: Some wild mushrooms contain toxins that can be lethal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Exposure to lethal concentrations of air pollutants highlights the importance of strict industrial safety regulations.

words.definitionEn: careless, improper, or illegal professional conduct, especially in medicine
words.exampleDailyEn: The family consulted a lawyer about possible medical malpractice.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Independent oversight can help prevent malpractice in healthcare and strengthen public confidence in medical institutions.

words.definitionEn: to provide what a living thing needs to grow healthily
words.exampleDailyEn: These simple meals nourish us after long working days.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can nourish children's curiosity by encouraging questions and providing opportunities for independent exploration.

words.definitionEn: to cause someone to lose the ability to move
words.exampleDailyEn: The injury paralysed his legs, but his arms remained strong.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Severe flooding can paralyse urban transport systems, preventing essential workers from reaching hospitals and other services.

words.definitionEn: A natural tendency to develop a particular illness or condition.
words.exampleDailyEn: My doctor explained that a predisposition does not guarantee illness.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although genetic predisposition influences the risk of diabetes, regular exercise and a balanced diet can offer protection.

words.definitionEn: happening before the expected or appropriate time
words.exampleDailyEn: Our celebration was premature; the match wasn't over yet.
words.exampleIeltsEn: It would be premature to conclude that the policy has succeeded without examining its long-term effects.

words.definitionEn: Likely to experience something undesirable or behave a certain way
words.exampleDailyEn: My skin is prone to dryness in cold weather.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Coastal settlements are increasingly prone to flooding as sea levels rise and extreme storms become more frequent.

words.definitionEn: to happen again, especially repeatedly or after an interval
words.exampleDailyEn: If these headaches recur, please speak to your doctor.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Traffic congestion will continue to recur unless cities address the underlying causes of excessive car use.

words.definitionEn: a passage through which air reaches the lungs
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse checked that the patient's airway was clear.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Heavy traffic along a major airway requires careful coordination to keep aircraft safely separated.

words.definitionEn: To surgically remove all or part of a limb.
words.exampleDailyEn: The vet had to amputate the cat's badly injured leg.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Early treatment of severe infections can reduce the need to amputate limbs and improve patients' quality of life.

words.definitionEn: A blood vessel carrying blood away from the heart.
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor explained how blood flows through an artery.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The new railway will become a major transport artery connecting rural communities with regional markets.

words.definitionEn: Quick and energetic.
words.exampleDailyEn: A brisk walk before breakfast always wakes me up.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular brisk walking can improve cardiovascular health without requiring expensive equipment or access to specialist facilities.

words.definitionEn: Strong, flexible tissue found in joints and other body parts.
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor explained that cartilage cushions my knee joint.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular moderate exercise can support joint health, but damaged cartilage often takes a long time to heal.

words.definitionEn: A powerful, addictive stimulant drug derived from coca leaves.
words.exampleDailyEn: The nurse explained why cocaine can seriously harm the heart.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public health programmes should combine education about cocaine with accessible treatment for people experiencing addiction.

words.definitionEn: To make someone unable to hear, temporarily or permanently.
words.exampleDailyEn: The sudden blast of the horn nearly deafened me.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Prolonged exposure to loud industrial machinery can deafen workers unless effective hearing protection is consistently provided.

words.definitionEn: the muscle below your lungs that helps you breathe
words.exampleDailyEn: The singing teacher explained how the diaphragm supports breathing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and moves downward, allowing the lungs to expand as air enters.

words.definitionEn: An insulting term for someone who is frequently drunk.
words.exampleDailyEn: The novel portrays the lonely innkeeper as a drunkard.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Calling someone a drunkard can reinforce stigma and discourage them from seeking professional help for alcohol dependence.

words.definitionEn: the complete removal or destruction of something harmful
words.exampleDailyEn: Complete eradication of these weeds will take patience.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The eradication of infectious diseases requires sustained investment in vaccination programmes and public health infrastructure.

words.definitionEn: Physical or mental effort, especially when it makes you tired.
words.exampleDailyEn: He was breathless from the exertion of climbing upstairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity benefits health, but excessive exertion without adequate recovery can increase the risk of injury.

words.definitionEn: Passed from parents to children through genes.
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor asked whether the condition might be hereditary.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Genetic counselling can help families understand hereditary conditions and make informed decisions about their healthcare.

words.definitionEn: A hospital or room providing medical care within an institution.
words.exampleDailyEn: The school nurse treated my ankle in the infirmary.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A well-equipped school infirmary allows minor injuries to be treated promptly without disrupting students' education.

words.definitionEn: a condition involving difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep
words.exampleDailyEn: His insomnia left him awake long after midnight again.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Persistent insomnia can affect concentration at work and may require advice from a healthcare professional.

words.definitionEn: To walk unevenly because one leg or foot is hurt
words.exampleDailyEn: I had to limp home after twisting my ankle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Athletes who continue to limp after an injury should receive professional assessment before returning to competitive sport.

words.definitionEn: poor health caused by insufficient or unbalanced nutrients
words.exampleDailyEn: The rescued kitten needed special food to treat malnutrition.
words.exampleIeltsEn: School meal programmes can reduce childhood malnutrition by providing balanced diets to children from low-income households.

words.definitionEn: an unusually strong enthusiasm for an activity or object
words.exampleDailyEn: A mania for collecting toy trains swept our neighbourhood.
words.exampleIeltsEn: During episodes of mania, individuals may need professional support to manage sleep disruption and impulsive behaviour.

words.definitionEn: a sleep-inducing painkiller; also an illegal drug
words.exampleDailyEn: The doctor prescribed a narcotic for severe pain after surgery.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Strict controls on narcotic medicines should prevent misuse without limiting access for patients with severe pain.

words.definitionEn: Either of the two openings at the bottom of the nose.
words.exampleDailyEn: One nostril felt blocked when I woke this morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Air entering through each nostril is warmed and filtered before it reaches the lungs.

words.definitionEn: loss of the ability to move part or all of the body
words.exampleDailyEn: The injury caused temporary paralysis in his left leg.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Political disagreements can lead to administrative paralysis, delaying essential decisions on housing and public transport.

words.definitionEn: Make someone unable to move all or part of their body.
words.exampleDailyEn: Some spinal injuries can paralyze both of a person's legs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Severe flooding can paralyze urban transport networks, preventing workers from reaching essential services and workplaces.

words.definitionEn: To swell or become larger because of pressure from inside.
words.exampleDailyEn: Too much gas can distend your stomach after meals.
words.exampleIeltsEn: During digestion, excess gas may distend the abdomen, causing discomfort that can affect daily activities.
